A short thread of things that have improved my agency. Prompted by @warrenkrettek — thank you, Warren, this is a great question!

===

1438364129312575489 [2021-09-16] @blisstweeting 💜 15
5.1. Challenges of various sorts may help you to boost your agency. The "do it 100 times" framework is near perfect for starting such challenges for yourself. https://t.co/3FBK2ttf3M
  [Quoting @visakanv: 1. Do it 100 times.   Write 100 songs, cook 100 omelettes, talk to 100 people. It never seems like a huge deal until you try it yourself. It’s manageable, and yet it stretches you, and you’ll be observably different at the end of it. Effective way to get a foothold on a new thing]
↓
1438364216176660482 [2021-09-16] @blisstweeting 💜 6
6. Improve coordination between your IFS parts.
↓
1438364718658379777 [2021-09-16] @blisstweeting 💜 7
7. Be ready to change. Embrace change.
↓
1438496391223984128 [2021-09-16] @blisstweeting 💜 8
8. Oh, and don't be too serious about yourself! It may not be obvious but by doing so you set up expectations for yourself that are stringent and that may impair your ability to diverge from the chosen path even if it's not optimal for your goals anymore.
↓
1438859772577697798 [2021-09-17] @blisstweeting 💜 6
9. I also believe that even simply thinking about agency helps improve it.
↓
1438909778969911299 [2021-09-17] @blisstweeting 💜 2
Addendum to 8. "Be flexible" is the message here. https://t.co/oVy1iJqrND
  [Quoting @blisstweeting: @AskYatharth To be precise, it's probably good to have intermittent periods of self-seriousness that sets high bar. It's just that one must avoid being enthralled by it.]
↓
1449509763704836099 [2021-10-16] @blisstweeting 💜 6
10a. Recognize your petty tyrants.
10b. Become unswayable by them. https://t.co/zpP0jVZNLH
  [Quoting @blisstweeting: I think we all have people who Carlos Castaneda called petty tyrants. Even if involuntary and unwittingly, they annoy and attack you nonetheless. One of the greatest achievements on the path of agency is when you become invincible to your petty tyrant's attacks.]
↓
1451285713740255232 [2021-10-21] @blisstweeting 💜 3
11. Don't focus *too* much on agency.
↓

↓

A corollary: you are only ever as agentic as your political theory says is the upper bound of rational agency.  Don't hand over your agency just like that. It's a mistake. It's really yours to keep. 16. Rereading this thread once in a while helps to boost agency too!

1477739838447095809 [2022-01-02] @danallison 💜 4
I think that crafting new year's resolutions is a special form of game design. Achieving goals is cool and all, but it's really more about creating new forms of agency.Images are from the book Games: Agency As Art by @add_hawk https://t.co/wBLwx9loME
Images:
  - [Image #0] The image shows a page from a book titled "Agency as Art." The text is transcribed as follows:
    
    **1 Agency as Art**
    
    Games can seem like an utterly silly way to spend one's time. We struggle and strain and sweat—and for what? The goals of games seem so arbitrary. Game players burn energy and effort, not on curing cancer or saving the environment, but on trying to beat each other at some unnecessary, invented activity. Why not spend that time on something real?
    
    But the goals of a game aren't actually arbitrary at all. They only seem arbitrary when we look in the wrong place. In the rest of life, we are used to justifying our goals by looking at the value of the goals themselves or by looking forward, to what follows from those goals. But with the goals of games, we often need to look backward. We need to look at the value of the activity of pursuing those goals. In ordinary practical life, we usually take the means for the sake of the ends. But in games, we can take up an end for the sake of the means. Playing games can be a motivational inversion of ordinary life.
↓
